project_type: Python report generator: JSON data -> Jinja2 HTML -> WeasyPrint PDF, with a pixel/word/colour fidelity harness (compare.py) against original PDFs
build_system: pip + python -m module invocation. No compiled build. WeasyPrint needs Pango (present) and font files.
test_framework: No unit test framework yet. Verification is done via scripts/compare.py which renders both PDFs to images and reports pixel-diff %, missing/extra words, and per-page fill colours.
build_command: pip install -r requirements.txt (run pyenv global 3.11.15 first). Render a report with: python -m sars_pdf.render <data.json> --pdf <out.pdf> [--html <out.html>]
test_command: python scripts/compare.py <original.pdf> <generated.pdf> --out <dir> --pages-out <dir>  (verdict = low pixel diff, 0/near-0 missing+extra words, matching fills)
verification_instructions: For each report: render its data.json to a PDF, then run compare.py against its reference/original.pdf. Success = generated PDF matches the original: same rows, same colours, same fonts, same everything (drive pixel-diff and word-diff toward 0 as in the existing lakezone example). Confirm the existing lakezone example still renders unchanged.
snapshot_or_generated_files: output/report.pdf, output/report.html, output/pages/page_NN.png, output/comparison/page_NN.png and output/comparison/README.md are generated artifacts checked into git. New per-report generators produce analogous artifacts under each report's own output/ (or a reports/.../output/ dir). Regenerate with the render + compare commands above.
setup_instructions: cd /projects/sandbox/sars-pdf; pyenv global 3.11.15; pip install -r requirements.txt (add pymupdf for PDF inspection during data extraction). Install real/metric-compatible fonts (see environment_constraints). Extract inputs: unzip -o council_pdf.zip -d council_pdf; unzip -o region_pdf.zip -d region_pdf (already extracted to council_pdf/council_pdf/ and region_pdf/region_pdf/).
environment_constraints: Network mode OPEN_INTERNET: pip install and font downloads are allowed. FONT DECISION POINT: the input PDFs embed genuine ArialMT, Arial-BoldMT, ArialNarrow-Bold, TimesNewRomanPS-BoldMT. These Monotype fonts are proprietary and cannot be freely/legally redistributed into the repo. No Arial/Times/Liberation fonts are currently installed on the host. The user requires REAL fonts with NO fallback chains. Approach: acquire real font FILES and register them via @font-face under the exact family names the CSS references ('Arial', 'Arial Narrow', 'Times New Roman') so the CSS carries a single family name with no fallback list. If genuine licensed Arial/Times files cannot be obtained in-sandbox, use metric-compatible open substitutes (Liberation Sans/Arimo for Arial, Liberation Sans Narrow for Arial Narrow, Liberation Serif/Tinos for Times New Roman) bundled as the @font-face src, and DOCUMENT this substitution clearly as a blocker note for the PR body. Do NOT invent a CSS fallback stack; each @font-face maps one family name to one real file.
contribution_requirements: Preserve the existing lakezone example end-to-end as the reference success case (README.md, data/lakezone_f2_mock_aug2026.json, templates/report.*, sars_pdf/*, scripts/compare.py, output/*). Do NOT delete or regress it. The orchestrator handles commit/push/PR; do not push. .github/workflows/compare.yml currently targets the single lakezone report.
key_patterns: Data stored as DISPLAY STRINGS (preserve exact number formatting like '70.4','65.00','100'). Fixed column fills live in CSS :root; only the COMPETENCY LEVEL cell is data-driven (grading.py maps GPA->A-F band and hence colour). render.py: JSON -> build_context (adds computed labels, competency level per row/overall) -> Jinja2 -> WeasyPrint. SCOPES map: LAKEZONEWISE->Z/RANK, REGIONWISE->R/RANK, COUNCILWISE->C/RANK, WARDWISE->W/RANK. Each new report is its OWN self-contained unit (own template.html.j2, own style.css, own data.json, own reference/original.pdf) per user instruction; do not force sharing unless genuinely a repeat of the same structure. Naming convention (per user steering): name templates/reports by LEVEL + WHAT-IT-DOES, not by location/proper-noun (e.g. 'council-schools-rank-subjectwise', 'region-top-10-schools'), so they are reusable for any future data.
relevant_files: README.md (whole philosophy: data model, palette, per-table quirks, fidelity check, scope->rank mapping)
sars_pdf/grading.py (GPA->competency band, the only conditional colour)
templates/report.html.j2, templates/report.css (the proven subjectwise-rank layout to reuse for the structurally-identical council/region subject-rank reports)
scripts/compare.py (fidelity harness/verdict, extend to per-report comparison)
data/lakezone_f2_mock_aug2026.json (display-string data model example - the SUCCESS EXAMPLE, keep intact)
region_pdf/region_pdf/*.pdf (12 region-level source PDFs; the two 'Schools Rank For Governments' files are byte-identical duplicates)
directory_structure: Existing: sars_pdf/ (render.py, grading.py), templates/ (report.html.j2, report.css), data/, scripts/ (compare.py), reference/ (original.pdf placeholder), output/. Inputs extracted to council_pdf/council_pdf/ and region_pdf/region_pdf/. PLANNED reorg: reports/secondary/{council,region}/<level-plus-function>/ each holding template.html.j2, style.css, data.json, reference/original.pdf, output/. reports/primary/ left as a documented placeholder for future work. Existing top-level lakezone example stays where it is as the success reference.

report_families.note: Council and region collections contain parallel report TYPES. Several council<->region pairs share the same structure (per user steering). Region variants of school-rank add a COUNCIL column and dual C/RANK + R/RANK columns.
report_families.schools-rank-subjectwise: Per-subject school ranking; STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL to existing lakezone example. Council: 'MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK SUBJECTWISE' (24pp). Region: 'Mwanza School Rank-EDK' (1pp), 'Mwanza School Rank-English Language' (6pp) - region adds COUNCIL col + C/RANK & R/RANK.
report_families.subjects-rank: One row per subject. Council: 'MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK' (2pp). Region: 'Mwanza Overall Subjects Performance' (2pp).
report_families.schools-rank-overall: Division-performance grid (F/M/T triplets, divisions I-IV + 0, I-III, I-IV, GPA). Council: 'MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK' (1pp, adds ward + C/R ranks). Region: 'Mwanza schools rank Overall' (6pp), 'Mwanza Schools Rank For Governments' (4pp, government schools only).
report_families.top-10-schools: Top 10 schools overall, division grid. Council: 'MWANZA CC 10 BEST SCHOOLS' (3pp, has multiple sections incl DISTRICTWISE/govt). Region: 'Mwanza Top 10 Schools' (6pp).
report_families.best-students-overall: Top students with per-candidate detailed subject list. Council: 'MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS' (5pp). Region: 'Mwanza Best Students-Overall' (9pp, adds COUNCIL col).
report_families.best-students-subjectwise: Top 10 students per subject. Council: 'MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS SUBJECTWISE' (30pp). Region: 'Mwanza Best students-Subjectwise' (23pp, adds COUNCIL col).
report_families.wards-rank: COUNCIL ONLY. Ward performance summary + per-ward rows. 'MWANZA CC Wards Rank' (1pp).
report_families.district-performance: REGION ONLY. Per-council/district division grid. 'Mwanza f2 District Performance' (5pp).
report_families.mobility: REGION ONLY. 2025 vs 2026 GPA movement (IMEPANDA/UMESHUKA/etc). 'Mwanza f2 Mock Mobility 2026' (6pp).
report_families.page_orientation: Most council/region reports are LANDSCAPE (792x612pt). Exceptions PORTRAIT (612x792pt): 'MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK SUBJECTWISE', 'Mwanza School Rank-EDK', 'Mwanza School Rank-English Language', 'Mwanza f2 Mock Mobility 2026'.
report_families.fonts_embedded: ArialMT, Arial-BoldMT, ArialNarrow-Bold, TimesNewRomanPS-BoldMT (council). Region PDFs use subsetted CIDFonts (same visual families).
